chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a person in Ihram who looked at his wife and discharged semen or seminal fluid while he was in Ihram. He said: There is nothing upon him, but let him perform Ghusl and seek forgiveness from his Lord.
And if he carried her without desire, so he discharged semen or seminal fluid, then there is nothing upon him.
And if he carried her or touched her with desire, so he discharged semen or seminal fluid, then upon him is Dam (blood of a sacrificial animal).
And he said regarding the one in Ihram who looks at his wife and descends upon her with desire until he discharges, said: Upon him is a Badana (a young female camel).

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A young female camel used as sacrifice
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood, referring to a sacrificial animal
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: A pilgrim in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim in Ihram who has sexual intercourse with his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the graduated penalties (kaffarah) for a pilgrim in Ihram who engages in sexual intimacy with his wife, distinguishing between mere looking, touching, and intercourse, as well as the presence or absence of sexual desire. It establishes that while looking without desire incurs no penalty, intercourse requires a camel (Badana), reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the degree of distraction from the sacred state. The ruling underscores the spiritual gravity of maintaining focus during Hajj, linking physical acts to specific compensatory sacrifices.
